purpose: package the application and its runtime into a small, secure, reproducible container image
entry_criteria: Application builds and runs outside a container
procedure: Write a Dockerfile with a pinned, minimal base image and a multi-stage build so build tools do not ship.
Run as a non-root user, copy only what the application needs, and keep secrets out of layers and build arguments.
Define the entrypoint, health check, exposed ports and resource expectations.
Build the image in CI, tag it by commit, and record its digest.
Run the container locally or in CI and verify it starts, passes the health check and shuts down cleanly on a termination signal.
Hand the digest to container security scanning (stage 102).
acceptance_criteria: No secrets in layers or build arguments
Container starts, is healthy and stops cleanly
Base image and tools are pinned
validation_method: Platform and security review of the Dockerfile.

validation.command: docker build -t app:test . && docker run --rm -d --name t app:test && sleep 5 && docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}' t

failure_modes.mode: Build tools shipped in the final image

failure_modes.detection: Takes the kill timeout to stop
failure_modes.response: Handle the signal; run the process as PID 1 correctly

failure_modes.mode: Secret passed as a build argument
failure_modes.response: Use build secrets and rotate it

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A two-stage Dockerfile compiles in a builder image and copies only the binary into a minimal base running as user 10001. The container reports healthy within five seconds and stops on SIGTERM in under a second.
